title: Verranza Coastal Retreats villa portfolio: neutralize twelve mixed-light HDR frames across three properties to one house white point via an in-frame grey card, balance a blown sea-view window, vectorize the collection wordmark, then data-merge one press-ready listing sheet per villa
grounding_note: Adapted from a real Upwork real-estate HDR-finishing brief (a boutique Caribbean vacation-rental manager wanting 'a consistent, premium visual identity across the whole portfolio' with a 'natural, realistic look' and an explicit DO-NOT-WANT list: no fake-HDR, no over-saturation, no unrealistically-blue pools) and laundered to a fictional collection, 'Verranza Coastal Retreats' on the fictional cove of Anse Verranza — no real company, place, product, capture-workflow vendor, or trademark is named anywhere. REPOSITIONED away from the killed original: the killed spec ran three independent 4-6 call tonal chains and openly CONCEDED that perspective/vertical warp and cable/stain cloning were 'left as the human's finishing pass', so it disclaimed the paid design work to a human and was functionally identical to the shipped adobe-batch-edit-photos skill. This rebuild removes every human handoff — the connector does the ENTIRE job — and repositions it as what the merge tool genuinely produces: a per-villa property LISTING SHEET (one press-ready single-record sheet per property) for the collection's booking brochure. The client supplies a genuinely hand-authored InDesign single-record listing-sheet template (.indd, NOT a converted PDF) carrying live <<fields>> AND THREE @-prefixed image-path columns (an exterior hero, a key interior, and the collection wordmark), a three-row property roster CSV, twelve raw HDR frames (four per villa) shot across the three properties under mismatched light each with a photographic 18% grey card laid in one corner as a neutral reference, and a flat wordmark scan on off-white stock. The Adobe chain does the real work the brief rewards: neutralize every one of the twelve frames to its own in-frame grey card so all three properties share ONE house white point (interiors shot warm, exteriors shot cool, one terrace shot at genuine golden hour), recover a blown bright sea-view window on one interior via a masked local pull without wrecking the lifted room, prep-and-vectorize the scanned wordmark, then run the authored template through a one-file-per-row data-merge and export a press-ready listing sheet per villa. The DO-NOT-WANT list is honored by neutralizing to a real reference and holding restraint (a subtle warm house tone, per-band saturation only) rather than a global pump.
one_line_ask: Finish a three-villa vacation-rental portfolio: neutralize twelve mixed-lighting HDR frames (four per property) to the 18% grey card each one carries so all three villas read as one matched, premium set, deciding per frame how far to move white balance and exposure to hit the shared house target; recover a blown bright sea-view window on one interior with a masked local pull; prep and vectorize the collection wordmark; then data-merge the client's authored single-record listing template against the property roster to produce one press-ready listing sheet per villa.
full_brief: Verranza Coastal Retreats manages a collection of luxury vacation-rental villas and needs a consistent, premium look across the whole portfolio for our booking brochure. We are NOT reshooting. For this batch we are handing you three properties, four hero frames each — twelve HDR frames in all — and here is the problem: they came out of a standard real-estate HDR workflow already roughly exposed but they do NOT match. The interiors were shot under warm indoor light, the pool and exterior frames under cooler daylight, and one terrace was shot at late-afternoon golden hour — so straight out of the folder the twelve read as a jumble of casts, and a brochure where every villa has a different color feel looks cheap. To make consistency checkable, the shooter clipped a photographic 18% grey card into one corner of every frame as a neutral reference. Your job on the photos: bring all twelve to one consistent, true-to-property look by neutralizing each frame to the grey card it contains — the card must read as a clean neutral grey (equal across the channels) in your finished frame, and once every card is neutral the whole portfolio shares one house white point. Hold a subtle warm, inviting house tone in the final look, but do NOT force one blanket correction across the batch: each frame was lit differently and needs its own white-balance, exposure and tone decision to land on the shared target — some frames need warming, others cooling, one interior is shot through greenish work-light and needs a tint move plus a real exposure lift, one facade is over-exposed and needs recovery, and pushing the same numbers through all twelve will leave the set mismatched. Keep it natural and realistic — never a fake-HDR, over-saturated, or unnaturally-blue-pool result; enhance the water and sea by lifting the blue/cyan band specifically rather than pumping global saturation. On the living-room interior of the first villa, the bright sea-view window is blown out; recover the view through it by pulling that window down LOCALLY while keeping the room itself lifted and bright — do not simply darken the whole frame or the room goes muddy. When you are done, tell us the final white-balance and exposure move you made on each of the twelve frames so we can confirm the set was matched to one target, not eyeballed frame by frame. Second, our collection wordmark only exists as a flat scan on off-white paper — get it clean and razor-sharp as a vector for the sheet masthead; it must not look like a fuzzy scan when printed. Finally, build the brochure: we have hand-built the InDesign listing-sheet template with the real placeholder fields and three image slots (an exterior hero window, an interior window, and the wordmark at the masthead) and we are giving you the property roster; merge them so every villa gets its own single-page listing sheet with its name, location, bedroom/sleeps count, weekly rate and description bound in, its exterior hero and a key interior dropped into the two photo windows, and the crisp wordmark in the masthead — then hand back one press-ready ~300 DPI listing brochure covering every property, one page per villa. Bind the copy verbatim from the roster; do not rewrite our descriptions or rates. Acceptance: every grey card neutral and the whole twelve-frame set matched to one house white point; the sea-view window recovered locally with the room still bright; the wordmark a crisp vector; every photo that lands in a sheet still sharp at print size in its window; and exactly one finished listing sheet per property row.

inputs.name: verranza_listing_template.indd
inputs.gen_prompt: AUTHORED DELIVERABLE (cannot be model-generated): a genuine, hand-built Adobe InDesign document (.indd/.idml) for a SINGLE-RECORD A4 landscape villa listing sheet — ONE property per page — with 3 mm bleed. It must contain live InDesign data-merge placeholder fields <<property_name>>, <<location>>, <<bedrooms>>, <<sleeps>>, <<weekly_rate>>, <<description>>, and THREE @-prefixed image-path merge columns wired to three separate image frames: a large exterior-hero photo window (~90 x 60 mm, 3:2) bound to @hero, a secondary interior photo window (~100 x 75 mm, 4:3) bound to @interior, and a masthead logo frame bound to @wordmark. Because free-form image-at-coordinates placement is banned, BOTH photos and the wordmark reach their windows ONLY as merge binds through these three image columns — nothing is dropped in by hand. The <<description>> frame has Auto-Size 'shrink text to fit' enabled so a long villa description binds without going overset. Built by hand in InDesign so the merge fields and ALL THREE image fields actually bind. Explicitly NOT a convert_pdf_to_indd output and NOT a multi-record grid: document_merge_data_layout emits one file per row, so the template holds exactly one property's worth of fields; a converted-PDF template has no live merge fields or data-merge image fields and would not bind, and a multi-up grid cannot be produced.
inputs.realism_notes: document_merge_data_layout is [T] and REQUIRES a user-authored .indd carrying real merge fields plus genuine @image-path columns, and it emits ONE FILE PER ROW — so a single-record per-villa listing sheet is the correct, connector-doable shape (three rows => three sheets), not a multi-up catalog. Supplied as an input, not a chain output. THREE @image-path columns (@hero, @interior, @wordmark) extend the proven two-image-column merge pattern by one more column of the same kind: each is an ordinary @-prefixed image-path column, so the merge resolves three prepped assets per row — the villa's graded exterior hero, its graded key interior, AND the shared vectorized wordmark — giving both the per-row photos and the chain-produced wordmark a real, connector-doable path onto every sheet without any free-form placement. Column names must exactly match the roster headers and the template fields.

inputs.name: verranza_property_roster.csv
inputs.gen_prompt: Generate a CSV with headers exactly: property_name,location,bedrooms,sleeps,weekly_rate,description,@hero,@interior,@wordmark and exactly 3 property rows, one per villa: (1) 'Casa Verranza' — a hillside villa with an infinity pool and sea-view living room; (2) 'Villa Solene' — a garden villa with an open kitchen-living space and a shaded terrace; (3) 'Maison Aurel' — a modern facade villa with a bright living room and dining terrace. Each row carries a fictional location on the fictional cove of Anse Verranza, a bedrooms count (e.g. 4), a sleeps count (e.g. 8), a weekly rate in US dollars (e.g. '$9,800 / week'), and a two-to-three sentence guest-facing description. The @hero column names that villa's graded exterior hero file (p1_hero_graded.jpg, p2_hero_graded.jpg, p3_hero_graded.jpg in row order); the @interior column names that villa's graded key-interior file (p1_living_graded.jpg, p2_living_graded.jpg, p3_living_graded.jpg); the @wordmark column holds the SAME vectorized wordmark file — verranza_wordmark.svg — in every row so the merge drops the one shared masthead mark onto every sheet as a merge bind (never free-form placement). Column names must exactly match the template merge fields <<property_name>>,<<location>>,<<bedrooms>>,<<sleeps>>,<<weekly_rate>>,<<description>> and the three @image-path columns @hero,@interior,@wordmark.
inputs.realism_notes: Three rows => the merge must produce exactly three finished listing sheets (page-count = row-count gate). The @hero / @interior columns hold the filenames the agent must produce and upload under those exact names, so naming discipline is a real dependency: the exterior hero and the key interior of the SAME villa must map to the same row. @wordmark carries the identical vectorized SVG path in all three rows, giving the chain-produced wordmark a connector-doable path onto every sheet via the merge (mirrors AO-74/AO-75's shared-wordmark-via-@column pattern, extended to a three-image-column sheet). Rates and descriptions bind verbatim; nothing is rewritten.

inputs.name: raw_villa_frames_x12.zip
inputs.gen_prompt: A set of 12 REAL full-frame DSLR/mirrorless real-estate HDR captures, each ~4000-4500 px on the long edge (full-resolution stills straight off the camera before any crop), each with a photographic 18% grey card laid flat in one corner of the frame as a neutral reference, grouped as four hero frames for each of three luxury Caribbean vacation villas. CASA VERRANZA: (1) infinity-pool exterior hero at midday under a slightly cool, hazy daylight cast, frame tilted ~3 deg, turquoise water reading a touch dull/greenish; (2) sea-view living room under warm tungsten interior light, the large window to the sea BLOWN OUT bright so the room reads dark by comparison; (3) master bedroom under the same warm tungsten light, level; (4) terrace looking out to sea at genuine late-afternoon GOLDEN HOUR — the whole scene is warmly, beautifully lit by the low sun and this warmth is REAL scene color, its grey card shot under that same neutral-to-the-sensor balance reads essentially neutral, frame tilted ~2 deg. VILLA SOLENE: (5) pool/garden exterior hero under cool blue overcast light, level, water muted; (6) open kitchen-living space under greenish fluorescent work-light AND slightly underexposed; (7) bedroom under warm window light, level; (8) shaded terrace with a muted teal sea and a flat pale sky, slightly underexposed, level. MAISON AUREL: (9) modern facade exterior hero, OVER-exposed near-daylight with hot blown highlights on the white render, level; (10) bright living room under cool LED light, flat and low-contrast, level; (11) bedroom under mixed warm-key / cool-fill light, only mildly off, level; (12) dining terrace at dusk under warm tungsten string-lights, level. Every frame has real architectural texture, stone/travertine/timber/fabric detail, real water ripples and reflections, candid documentary real-estate framing, no people, no CGI gloss. The grey card is clearly visible and uncropped in every frame.
inputs.realism_notes: REAL-CAMERA capture at ~4000-4500 px long edge (NOT an AI-gen ~1024-1536 px raster) precisely so every window crop fills its listing-sheet photo frame at ~300 DPI by DOWNSCALE ONLY — the ~90 x 60 mm hero window needs ~1063 x 709 px and the ~100 x 75 mm interior window ~1181 x 886 px, both reachable by downscale, never by upscale. Deliberately mismatched across the twelve (per-frame WB, exposure and tilt vary in opposite directions) so a single blanket correction cannot fix the set — each frame needs its own decision measured to its in-frame 18% grey card, the free checkable neutral target (inputs are generated, so it costs nothing). Frame 4 (Casa Verranza golden-hour terrace) is the TRAP: its warmth is real golden-hour scene light, not a cast, and its grey card already reads neutral, so cooling it (assuming 'warm = cast' as on the tungsten interiors) strips the very light the listing is selling. Frame 2 carries the blown sea-view window for the masked local recovery. Frame 6 is a two-axis problem (green tint + underexposure). Delivered as a zip of 12 individually addressable full-resolution JPEGs; the grey card is cropped out of every delivered crop but retained in each neutralized master for grading.

inputs.name: verranza_wordmark_scan.png
inputs.gen_prompt: A flat desktop scan of the 'Verranza Coastal Retreats' wordmark inked on off-white textured paper: an elegant thin high-contrast serif with a small palm-frond mark, deep charcoal lettering. Rendered as a scan — the paper is a slightly warm off-white (NOT transparent, NOT pure white), the whole thing sits very slightly rotated (~2 deg) on the scan bed, there is extra paper margin around the mark, and the edges are a touch soft as a real scan would be. High enough contrast that, once cleaned, it will vectorize cleanly. No gradients, no photographic texture in the letterforms.
inputs.realism_notes: Scanned-on-paper (off-white ground, slight rotation, margin, soft edges) so image_vectorize would trace the paper and the skew if fed raw — forcing genuine prep-before-trace: straighten, boost contrast/crispness so the charcoal separates hard from the ground, crop to the mark, knock the off-white ground to transparency, THEN vectorize. Flat solid-color lettering on light stock means the enclosed serif/counter shapes read as white after the knock (light-ground knockout is fine per the counter rule) and the trace stays clean. gemini-3-pro-image for legible lettering.

outputs.name: Verranza_Villa_Portfolio_Brochure_x3.pdf
outputs.spec: Exactly three press-ready A4 landscape villa listing sheets — ONE single-record sheet per roster row (page-count = row-count = 3) — exported from the one-file-per-row InDesign data-merge with 3 mm bleed at ~300 DPI; each sheet binds its property_name/location/bedrooms/sleeps/weekly_rate/description verbatim from the roster, drops that villa's grey-card-neutralized exterior hero into the @hero window (>=1063 x 709 px so it prints >=300 DPI) and its graded key interior into the @interior window (>=1181 x 886 px), and drops the vectorized collection wordmark into the masthead frame (via @wordmark) — all three by merge bind, never free-form placement.

outputs.name: graded_villa_frames_x12
outputs.spec: Twelve grey-card-neutralized, premium-finished HDR frames (four per villa), delivered as the window-framed crops (grey card cropped OUT) plus their RETAINED pre-crop neutralized masters (the *_neutralized full-res frames, grey card still in frame) which the harness keeps as the neutrality-grading artifacts. Acceptance (grader-checked, two SEPARATE claims): (a) neutralisation is graded on the RETAINED pre-crop neutralized master of each frame (its in-frame 18% grey card still present) — the card region reads a clean neutral (per-channel spread near zero) with all twelve frames matched to ONE shared house white point while holding a subtle warm house tone, and true-to-scene (no frame's genuine color forced off, the golden-hour terrace's warmth preserved); (b) card-exclusion is checked separately on each delivered window crop (the *_graded output) — framed on the property with the grey card fully cropped OUT (no card pixels present). The neutrality tolerance is NEVER evaluated on the card-removed crop. Water/sea enhanced by lifting the blue/cyan band specifically, not by a global saturation pump. Accompanied by a report of the final white-balance and exposure move applied to each of the twelve frames.

outputs.name: casa_verranza_living_windowbalanced.jpg
outputs.spec: The Casa Verranza sea-view living room with the blown bright window recovered by a MASKED local pull: image_select_by_prompt isolates the window, then a masked image_apply_adjustments pass pulls its highlights/whites down so the sea view returns THROUGH the glass, while the room around it stays lifted and bright from the whole-frame grade — not a whole-image darken (which would mud the room) and not a fake-HDR halo. This is the p1_living master that also feeds the @interior crop for the Casa Verranza sheet.

outputs.name: listing_hero_16x9.jpg
outputs.spec: A 16:9 booking-header hero, 1920 x 1080, cropped by honest downscale from a graded exterior neutralized master (existing pixels only, no canvas extend, no upscale) for the brochure cover / web header.

outputs.name: verranza_wordmark.svg
outputs.spec: Clean vector SVG of the collection wordmark, traced only after the scan is straightened, crisped, cropped to the mark, and knocked to transparency — razor-sharp at masthead scale with no captured paper ground or skew. Binds into every listing sheet's masthead via @wordmark.

outputs.name: grade_report.txt
outputs.spec: A plain parameter sheet the agent authors and returns: for each of the twelve frames, the white-balance temperature and tint, the exposure offset, and the key tonal move it applied, plus the single common house-target white point all twelve were matched to. This is the acceptance artifact that makes 'the portfolio is matched to one target' checkable — the corrections must be NON-identical across the warm interior, cool exterior, green-cast, over-exposed and golden-hour frames, and the golden-hour terrace must show WB held (not cooled).

connector_workflow.note: Triage: the Casa Verranza pool hero is tilted ~3 deg, so level it first. (Only the tilted frames 1/4 get straightened; the level frames skip this — deciding which is part of the job. This only levels a tilted horizon; no perspective/vertical warp is claimed or needed.)

Cool hazy daylight cast: WARM it slightly (positive temperature) and set tint until the in-frame 18% grey card reads neutral (R=G=B), add contrast/clarity to cut the haze, then lift the blue/cyan band specifically to bring the dull water toward a clean natural turquoise WITHOUT a global saturation pump (honors the no-unnaturally-blue-pool constraint). Reason the exact temperature/exposure to THIS card. Report the move. Single primitive-built adjustments call (replaces the deprecated image_adjust_color_temperature / _vibrance_and_saturation / _brightness_and_contrast).

Crop the neutralized frame to the 3:2 exterior-hero window ratio, framing on the pool/villa with the grey card cropped OUT, holding >=1063 x 709 px so it clears the 300 DPI floor for the @hero window. The pre-crop master (p1_hero_neutralized, card still in frame) is RETAINED as the neutrality-grading artifact; the card is graded THERE, card-exclusion is the separate check here. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only, never generative-expand.

Casa Verranza living room, warm tungsten cast: COOL it (negative temperature) until its grey card reads neutral on the shared white point, and LIFT the interior shadows/exposure so the room reads bright and inviting (the indoor side of the indoor/outdoor balance). Do NOT yet touch the blown window — that is the masked local step next. Report the move. This full-res neutralized master feeds BOTH the masked window recovery AND the @interior crop, so keep it before cropping.

Semantically select only the bright sea-view window ('the bright blown-out sea-view window'). A real object/part selection (allowed) — NOT a hue, geometric band, or coordinate selection — returning a maskURI so the recovery is confined to the glass and the lifted room is untouched.

Masked local recovery (consumes the room master + window mask): pull highlights/whites/exposure DOWN inside the window only so the sea view returns through the glass, while the room's lifted brightness from step 4 is left intact. image_apply_adjustments accepts a mask, so this is a genuine local edit — a whole-image darken would mud the room and break the indoor/outdoor balance. DELIVERABLE casa_verranza_living_windowbalanced.jpg and the source for the @interior crop.

Crop the window-balanced living room to the 4:3 interior window ratio, grey card cropped OUT, holding >=1181 x 886 px for the @interior window. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only. Binds into the Casa Verranza sheet.

Casa Verranza master bedroom, same warm tungsten light but a slightly different exposure from the living room: cool to neutralize its OWN grey card to the shared white point and lift to match the set — its numbers should be close to frame 2's but NOT copied, because the exposure differs. Report the move.
Crop to a gallery window ratio, grey card OUT. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only. Gallery deliverable (not bound into a sheet, but part of the matched twelve).
Casa Verranza golden-hour terrace tilted ~2 deg — level the sea horizon.

THE TRAP FRAME. This terrace is warm because it was shot at genuine golden hour — the warmth is REAL scene light, not a cast — and its in-frame grey card ALREADY reads neutral. The correct move is essentially NO white-balance shift (only match exposure/contrast to the set and gently lift the sea's blue band). An agent that batch-applies the 'cool the warm cast' correction used on the tungsten interiors 2/3, or that assumes any warm frame is mis-balanced, will neutralize this card OFF-neutral and strip the golden light the listing is selling. Decision must be driven by THIS card. Report that WB was HELD.
Crop to a gallery window ratio, grey card OUT. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only. Gallery deliverable.

Villa Solene pool/garden hero, cool blue overcast cast: warm to neutralize its grey card to the shared white point (a different magnitude from the Casa hazy frame because the light differs), lift the blue/cyan band to bring the muted water toward natural turquoise without a global pump. Report the move.
Crop to the 3:2 exterior-hero window, grey card OUT, >=1063 x 709 px. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only. Binds into the Villa Solene sheet via @hero.

Villa Solene kitchen-living space: a TWO-AXIS problem — greenish fluorescent work-light AND underexposed. The dominant colour move is on TINT (push toward magenta) to kill the green while neutralizing the grey card, PLUS a real exposure/shadow lift. A simple temperature slide alone will not neutralize a green cast. Land the card neutral on the shared white point. Report the move.
Crop to the 4:3 interior window, grey card OUT, >=1181 x 886 px. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only. Binds into the Villa Solene sheet via @interior.
Villa Solene bedroom, warm window light: cool toward neutral against its grey card to the shared white point; protect any window highlight from clipping. Report the move.
Crop to a gallery window ratio, grey card OUT. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only. Gallery deliverable.

Villa Solene shaded terrace, muted teal sea + flat pale sky + slightly underexposed: lift exposure and add natural contrast, neutralize its grey card to the shared white point, and lift the blue/cyan band consistently with the pool frame's water treatment so the property reads coherent. Report the move.
Crop to a gallery window ratio, grey card OUT. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only. Gallery deliverable.

Maison Aurel facade hero, OVER-exposed near-daylight with hot blown highlights on the white render: PULL exposure/highlights/whites DOWN to recover the render texture FIRST, then a small WB nudge so its grey card lands neutral on the shared white point. Tonal recovery dominates here — opposite direction from the underexposed frames 6/8. Report the move.
Crop to the 3:2 exterior-hero window, grey card OUT, >=1063 x 709 px. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only. Binds into the Maison Aurel sheet via @hero.

Maison Aurel living room, cool LED light + flat and low-contrast: warm to neutralize its grey card to the shared white point AND add contrast/clarity to give the flat frame life — a WB-plus-tonal move distinct from the others. Report the move.
Crop to the 4:3 interior window, grey card OUT, >=1181 x 886 px. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only. Binds into the Maison Aurel sheet via @interior.
Maison Aurel bedroom, mixed warm-key / cool-fill, only mildly off: a modest, careful correction to bring the grey card to neutral on the shared white point without overshooting. Report the move.
Crop to a gallery window ratio, grey card OUT. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only. Gallery deliverable.

Maison Aurel dining terrace at dusk under warm tungsten string-lights: this is a warm CAST (unlike the golden-hour trap frame 4) — cool it to neutralize its grey card to the shared white point while keeping the string-lights' glow warm and inviting. Report the move. Frames 1-12 now share one house white point, each neutralized to its own grey card.
Crop to a gallery window ratio, grey card OUT. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only. Gallery deliverable.

Honest 16:9 booking-header hero: crop the graded Casa Verranza pool master (full-res neutralized, step 2) to 1920 x 1080 by downscale — existing pixels only, grey card cropped out, never a canvas extend or upscale. DELIVERABLE listing_hero_16x9.jpg.
Prep-before-trace step 1: the scan sits ~2 deg rotated on the bed — straighten so the vector edges are square. Feeding the raw skewed scan to vectorize would bake in the rotation.

Prep-before-trace step 2: push contrast/clarity and drive the off-white paper toward white so the charcoal lettering separates hard from the ground — a soft low-contrast scan traces into ragged, doubled edges.
Prep-before-trace step 3: crop away the scan margin to the tight bounds of the mark so vectorize traces only the wordmark, not the paper field.

Prep-before-trace step 4: knock the off-white paper ground to transparency so the trace captures the letterforms only, not a rectangle of paper. remove_background -> transparency (NOT select->invert->fill). On this LIGHT ground the enclosed serif counters read as white, so the knockout stays clean (no dark-ground counter problem).

Trace the prepared raster (straightened, crisped, cropped, transparent) into a clean SVG for the masthead. Tracing the raw scan instead would produce a skewed, paper-bounded, fuzzy silhouette — the trap this prep chain avoids. DELIVERABLE verranza_wordmark.svg.

connector_workflow.inputs_from: p1_hero_graded, p1_living_graded, p2_hero_graded, p2_living_graded, p3_hero_graded, p3_living_graded, verranza_wordmark.svg
connector_workflow.note: Initialize an upload session for the six sheet-bound crops (each villa's exterior hero + key interior) plus the vector wordmark so the merge can resolve them by the @hero, @interior and @wordmark columns. Files uploaded under the exact names the roster references (e.g. p1_hero_graded.jpg for Casa Verranza's @hero, verranza_wordmark.svg for @wordmark). The other six gallery crops are delivered but not bound into a sheet, so they are not part of the merge upload.
Finalize the upload; returns the asset URNs the roster's @hero / @interior / @wordmark columns resolve to for each villa's single-record listing sheet.

One-file-per-row InDesign data-merge: bind each of the three roster rows (property_name/location/bedrooms/sleeps/weekly_rate/description) into the authored SINGLE-RECORD .indd's live <<fields>> and resolve ALL THREE image columns per row — drop that villa's graded exterior hero into the @hero window, its graded key interior into the @interior window, and the shared vectorized wordmark (from @wordmark, identical in every row) into the masthead frame — producing EXACTLY ONE merged sheet per row (three sheets); the auto-fit description frame shrinks long copy. Binding the two photos and the wordmark through @image columns is the ONLY connector-doable path — free-form image-at-coordinates placement is banned. [T] requires the hand-authored template. A convert_pdf_to_indd template or a multi-up grid would not bind / cannot be produced — this is the correct shape.

Export the merged single-record sheets to a press-ready ~300 DPI A4 landscape + 3 mm bleed PDF, one listing sheet per villa. document_render_layout exports the WHOLE merged multi-page document (all three sheets, one page per property) in a single call — it cannot export one named record on its own, so there is no per-record named export. Acceptance: page-count = row-count = 3; if fewer, the merge collapsed rows and failed.

chaining_note: Strict output-to-input chaining across twelve per-frame grade sub-chains and three converging asset streams. Each of the twelve frames fans out from the raw zip into an image_apply_adjustments neutralization driven to that frame's OWN in-frame 18% grey card (adaptive per frame: warm the cool hazy pool 1 and cool-overcast pool 5, cool the tungsten interiors 2/3/8-analogue and the dusk terrace 12, magenta-tint + lift the green/underexposed kitchen 6, lift the underexposed terrace 8, pull down the over-exposed facade 9, warm + add contrast the cool-flat LED living room 10, hold WB on the genuinely-golden terrace 4) so all twelve converge on ONE shared house white point, with image_auto_straighten inserted only on the tilted frames 1 and 4, then an image_crop_and_resize that crops the grey card OUT and reframes to the window ratio at the stated pixel floor. Casa Verranza's living room runs a masked local recovery: p1_living_neutralized (4) -> image_select_by_prompt window (5) -> masked image_apply_adjustments (6, window pulled down, room held) -> crop (7). The wordmark runs a genuine prep-before-trace chain: straighten (30) -> crisp adjustments (31) -> crop_to_bounds (32) -> remove_background to transparency (33) -> vectorize (34). The 16:9 header (29) is an honest downscale-crop of the Casa pool master. The six sheet-bound crops (each villa's @hero + @interior) and the wordmark SVG converge into the upload session (35) -> finalize (36) -> document_merge_data_layout (37), which also consumes the authored single-record .indd and the roster CSV and emits one merged sheet per row, resolving @hero (that villa's exterior), @interior (that villa's key interior) and @wordmark (the shared vector, identical in every row) into the template's three merge-wired image frames. The merged set is exported once by document_render_layout (38) to the single press-ready ~300 DPI A4 landscape PDF (three sheets, one page per villa); no per-record named export is attempted.
